_note: Structure follows Muijlwijk et al. (2024), Sec. 4.2.1 and 4.2.3. Items with source 'paper' are quoted from the paper. Items with source 'adapted' are placeholders written for this implementation: the paper does not print them. Replace their text with the original translated items (trust: McKnight et al. 2002; computer self-efficacy: Marakas et al. 2007) before running a real study. Item ids and scale ids are what the analysis uses, so keep them.

scales.title: Your experience with the model
scales.instruction: Please indicate to what extent you agree with the following statements.

items.text: The model performs its role of predicting marathon performances well.
The model is competent in setting finish times and pacing strategies.
The model is capable of predicting what a runner can achieve.
Overall, the model is effective in predicting marathon performances.
I feel I can count on the model when I need a suitable finish time and pace strategy.
When planning an important race, I would feel comfortable depending on the model.
I can always rely on the model for setting a finish time and pace strategy.
I would be willing to depend on the model when advising my runners.
If I had to set a suitable finish time and pace strategy, I would want to use the model again.
I would feel comfortable acting on the advice the model gives.
I would not hesitate to use the advice the model gives.
I would follow the model's advice for my runners.
I believe I am able to set a suitable finish time and pace strategy without the help of a model.
I believe I am able to determine which races are representative for a runner.
I believe I am able to adjust the model such that it gives a meaningful prediction.

scales.title: Working with computers
scales.instruction: How confident are you that you could do the following?

items.text: Learn to use a new software program without help from others.
Find out how to do something in a program by trying it myself.
Solve a problem when a program does not work as I expected.
Understand the main features of a new program quickly.
Use a program to analyse data, such as a spreadsheet.
Adjust the settings of a program to suit my needs.
As running coach I often use (calculation) models.
I regularly use tools or calculators to set target finish times.
I am experienced in analysing my runners' data.

demographics.text: What is your highest completed education?
How many years have you been a running coach?
How many years have you been running?
How many runners do you coach?
In how many marathons have you participated?
